module.name: fpvalgrind
module.short: Valgrind Helgrind and DRD client request annotations for custom synchronization primitives

descr.p: fpvalgrind provides lightweight inline client requests for the Valgrind thread error detectors (Helgrind and DRD). Use these routines to annotate user-space synchronization primitives that do not rely on POSIX pthread_mutex locks, such as spin locks (TSpinLock), lock-free atomic hand-offs, and recycled object caches.

On x86_64 targets using the System V ABI (Linux, BSD, Solaris, macOS), the routines emit the standard Valgrind client-request instruction sequence. When the program runs outside Valgrind, the sequence executes as a few register rotations with no side effects. On all other architectures and operating systems, the routines compile to empty no-op procedures.
In standard FCL units (syncobjs, system.threading), calls to fpvalgrind are guarded by the FPC_VALGRIND conditional define so that production builds incur zero overhead.

element.name: VgHappensBefore
element.short: Publishes memory writes performed by the calling thread associated with a synchronization tag

descr.p: VgHappensBefore emits the ANNOTATE_HAPPENS_BEFORE (VG_USERREQ__HG_USERSO_SEND_PRE) client request for the synchronization address aObj.

Call VgHappensBefore immediately before releasing a custom lock or setting an atomic completion flag. Any subsequent thread that observes the state change and calls with the same aObj pointer will inherit a happens-before edge in Helgrind and DRD, preventing false-positive data race reports on the protected data.

element.name: VgHappensBefore.aObj
element.short: Unique memory address identifying the synchronization object or atomic variable

element.name: VgHappensAfter
element.short: Acquires visibility of memory writes previously published with the same synchronization tag

descr.p: VgHappensAfter emits the ANNOTATE_HAPPENS_AFTER (VG_USERREQ__HG_USERSO_RECV_POST) client request for the synchronization address aObj.
Call VgHappensAfter immediately after acquiring a custom lock or observing an atomic completion flag that was preceded by .

element.name: VgHappensAfter.aObj
element.short: Unique memory address identifying the synchronization object or atomic variable

element.name: VgForgetAll
element.short: Discards all recorded happens-before tracking state for a synchronization address

descr.p: VgForgetAll emits the VG_USERREQ__HG_USERSO_FORGET_ALL client request for aObj. Call this routine before freeing or repurposing memory that served as a synchronization tag.

element.name: VgCleanMemory
element.short: Resets shadow memory access history for a recycled memory block

descr.p: VgCleanMemory emits the VALGRIND_HG_CLEAN_MEMORY client request for the range [aStart, aStart + aLen).

Use VgCleanMemory when an allocator or lock-free object pool (such as TThreadPool.TObjectCache) hands out a recycled object to a new thread without going through the system heap manager (malloc/free). This informs Helgrind that accesses by previous owners of the memory block must not be compared against accesses by the new owner.

element.name: VgCleanMemory.aStart
element.short: Starting address of the memory range to clean

element.name: VgCleanMemory.aLen
element.short: Length in bytes of the memory range

element.name: VgBenignRace
element.short: Disables data-race reporting on an intentionally lock-free or polled memory range

descr.p: VgBenignRace emits the VALGRIND_HG_DISABLE_CHECKING (VG_USERREQ__HG_ARANGE_MAKE_UNTRACKED) client request for the range [aStart, aStart + aLen).
Use VgBenignRace sparingly, and only for fields that are intentionally read without a lock as an optimistic fast path or monotonic status hint (for example, loop exit flags or adaptive stride hints).

element.name: VgBenignRace.aStart
element.short: Starting address of the untracked field

element.name: VgBenignRace.aLen
element.short: Size in bytes of the untracked field

element.name: VgRunningOnValgrind
element.short: Returns True when the process is executing under Valgrind

descr.p: VgRunningOnValgrind queries VG_USERREQ__RUNNING_ON_VALGRIND and returns True if the current process is supervised by Valgrind, or False when running natively or on an unsupported target.

element.name: VgRunningOnValgrind.Result
element.short: True if running under Valgrind, False otherwise
